question: Which recoil-named values in the weapon registry and related files are not yet described in the Frosty docs, whether or not the site models them?
method: Decoded GRX_Weapons on 2.1.2.0, tallied every GS_* row whose leaf name contains Recoil or ByOrder by value, and compared the leaf names with the text of docs/frosty, docs/working and the Analyzer docs. Row values are registry values; no GS file was re-read for this survey.
points: VerticalRecoilMultiplierByOrder and HorizontalRecoilMultiplierByOrder (per-shot-order multiplier lists) exist for both aim states of every GS root and are empty on all 142 rows each. With RecoilPatternSeed 0, RecoilPatternMultiplierPitch / Yaw 0, RecoilFadeOutStart / End -1, RecoilFadeOutFactor 1 and FirstShotMultiplierVerticalRecoil 1 on all 142 rows, no weapon stores a fixed recoil pattern, a shot-order ramp, a fade-out or a first-shot multiplier.

CameraRecoilAmount / CameraRecoilWhenZoomedAmount are -1.4 / -0.625 on 64 of 71 GS roots. The four semi-automatic pistols (FiveSeven, G22, M18, M45A1) store -0.25 / -0.25, the two revolvers (RagingHunter, TRR8) +0.25 / +0.25 (opposite sign), and the Railgun 0 / 0. IdleCameraRecoilWhenZoomedAmount follows the zoomed value except on the Railgun (-1.0).
IdleCameraRecoilWhenZoomedAmountSwitchTime is 0.0333333 s (two 60 Hz frames) on 70 roots and 0 on the Railgun; CameraRecoilUseTimeSinceLastShot is true on 70 and false on the Railgun.
UsePolarRecoil is false only on the Railgun (both aim states). The Railgun is a battle pickup, not a primary weapon (operator, 24 November), so its different values do not bear on the site roster.

CameraRecoil.IdleSpringConstantSwitchTime (and the Damping / Exponent switch times, which share its value) tracks the fire rate: on 41 of 45 automatic and burst site weapons it equals the shot interval rounded up to whole 60 Hz frames, plus one frame (720 rpm: 5 + 1 frames = 0.1 s; 900 rpm: 0.0833 s; 600 rpm: 0.1167 s; 514 rpm: 0.1333 s). VZ61, MK24 and NSW4 store one frame less and the Z84M one frame more. Semi-automatic, bolt and pump weapons store values unrelated to their rate cap (bolt rifles 0.2 s, pistols 0.1 s, revolvers 0.3667 s). Reading: the camera layer uses its firing spring while shots keep arriving and switches to the idle spring one frame after the next shot was due (recoil-survey/switch-time-check.json).

The 0.0333 s amount switch time against the 33 ms recovery pause: the pause was a one-parameter diagnostic fitted on the September camera-method recordings. The 14 October AK-205 bullet-hole capture already tested it (L4040 fitChi2): fixed dead time 33 ms 208, factor scale 0.8 48, stored law 580; it fits bursts only. Bullet holes bypass the camera layer and the stored 0.0333 s is a camera-layer value that is the same on 70 roots whatever their fire rate, so it does not describe the aim recovery. Whether it produced the apparent pause in the camera-based September readings is untested (it would need the camera spring equation).

Row names carry designer annotations for visual firing-animation modifiers that the docs do not describe: 'Tango6T 60% Push/Kick on bolts', 'Less kick/push for Canted RDS with NX8-4' / 'NX8-1', 'Procedural Firing 6.0x', and 'Proc Firing: Secondary Optic-specific Proc firing anim settings'. They attach to WeaponAnimationSettingsCombinableModifierBase records; the registry names no leaf value under them.

Related names seen on 23 November (L4086 receipt): the executable strings ProcVerticalRecoilKick, ProcHorizontalRecoilKick, ProcRecoilSettleAmount, ProcRecoilSettleTime, ProcRollRecoilKick, ProcRollRecoilKickSight and ProcRecoilPivotOffsetZ, and the animation states FB.Wep.Kickback.*, FB.Wep.PitchKick.*, FB.Wep.RecoilSettle.* and FB.Wep.RecoilDirection*.
inference: The visual weapon motion seen under compensation in the L4087 clips is a procedural firing animation with its own kick, settle and roll parameters, adjusted per optic by weapon-animation modifiers. Its values are not located.
unresolved: Where the procedural firing values are stored and which hashed fields they are; whether the camera-recoil amounts explain the size of the camera layer measured in L4045 / L4048.

assets.question: Which recoil-named GS rows are undocumented, and what do they hold?
assets.conclusion: Shot-order multiplier lists are empty on every weapon; camera-recoil amounts are uniform except pistols, revolvers and the Railgun; designer annotations name visual firing-animation modifiers.
